newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon journalist flees seeking asylum in France.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon journalist flees seeking asylum in France.

text.p: A Lebanese journalist charged with contacting Israeli agents has fled to France seeking asylum and will be tried in absentia by a military court in Beirut, his lawyer said on Thursday.
Attorney Boutros Harb said Pierre Atallah had left for France after being attacked and beaten by three unidentified men on the day he was officially charged in May.
"After the attack, he sneaked out of the country to France where he demanded to be granted the right to political asylum," Harb who is also an opposition MP, told a news conference.
Atallah, a reporter for the conservative newspaper an-Nahar, was charged six weeks ago with attempting to incite strife and slandering the army.

The indictment said investigations revealed that Attallah had developed strong ties with senior pro-Israeli militia leaders when he worked as a reporter for Middle East Television which broadcast inside Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone before joining an-Nahar in 1993.

"On May 14, the day the military magistrate issued the indictment, Pierre Atallah was beaten by three unknown men.... Two of them beat him in front of passersby and left him with deep wounds in his head and face," Harb said.
Atallah, a 34-year-old Christian, was one of 48 people rounded up in December after a van carrying Syrian workers came under machinegun fire in a mainly Christian area north of Beirut.
He was released 15 days later but was later charged with contacting Israeli agents.
Harb distributed photos allegedly documenting the attack on Atallah to journalists at the news conference. Atallah's face was severely bruised.
Harb said he had received a medical report on Atallah's health condition after the attack. He said he planned to open a court case on the incident.
Military magistrate Riad Talee' has demanded up to 15 years hard labour for Atallah.
Under a Lebanese 1974 law, only a special court that deals with crimes linked to publications is empowered to put journalists on trial.
The Paris-based press freedom watchdog group Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters without Borders) had appealed to Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri for Atallah's release.
